messages.subject: FeatureCounts crashes when QUAL = '*'
messages.body_plain:
FeatureCounts produces a segmentation fault when the QUAL score is '*'

This seems to be an acceptable value for the field given the documentation:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAM_(file_format)
QUAL: ASCII of base QUALity plus 33 (same as the quality string in the Sanger FASTQ format). A base quality is the phred-scaled base error probability which equals −10 log10 Pr{base is wrong}. This field can be a ‘*’ when quality is not stored. If not a ‘*’, SEQ must not be a ‘*’ and the length of the quality string ought to equal the length of SEQ.
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: Re: FeatureCounts crashes when QUAL = '*'
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

First, which version of featureCounts did you use?

I used featureCounts in the Subread-1.6.3 package, and it finished running on a SAM file with "*" in the SEQ field and "*" in the QUAL field.

Can you share with us your SAM file or a part of it (containing the header and thousands of alignments)?

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: FeatureCounts crashes when QUAL = '*'
messages.body_plain:
This causes a segmentation fault:

removing '*' fixes it:

samtools view -h ${outdir}_sorted.bam | awk '$3!="*" {print $0}' > cleaned.sam
featureCounts --verbose -t exon -g gene_id -a /mnt/biodata/genomes/Hsapiens/hg38/rnaseq/ref-transcripts.gtf -o counts.txt cleaned.sam
rm cleaned.sam

Perhaps there is another error with a read which also has a '*' for quality?

Bam file is available here:

https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Z16ZrckFFtBYSbYK6JaOjf-MJMKlR895

Cheers,
Andrew

messages.subject: Re: FeatureCounts crashes when QUAL = '*'
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

Thanks for the BAM file! I can now reproduce the error. The error is not about "*" in QUAL; it is because there are mapped reads in your BAM file that have "*" in the "RNAME" field, but has a cigar string containing "M" in the CIGAR field. In other words, the read is reported to be mapped but to no chromosome, while it has a mapped section. This is logically invalid, hence featureCounts crashed when it tried to use the chromosome name (a NULL pointer) for the mapped section.

Here is an example (I only included first 6 fields):

OBIWAN:364:CBYHYANXX:6:1204:1528:77185/1        16      *       345     60      126M    *

Although it said in BAM spec that "If RNAME is *, no assumptions can be made about POS and CIGAR.", I'm not sure why a mapped read (indicate by its FLAG field) can have no chromosome name.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: FeatureCounts crashes when QUAL = '*'
messages.body_plain: Given that the BAM specification allows a non-empty CIGAR string for a read mapped to no chromosome, we will allow it in featureCounts in the Subread-1.6.4 package, which will be soon released. Such reads will be put into the "Unassigned_NoFeatures" category in the summary output.
